newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish yields seen up in small investor interest.
newsitem.headline: Polish yields seen up in small investor interest.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields should continue their recent upward push at Monday's 1.3 billion zloty primary T-bill auction amid small interest from both foreigners and domestic corporates, dealers said on Friday.
They said the finance ministry was still strapped for cash and would probably be forced to accept higher yields next week.

"The upward trend in yields will remain intact. The finance ministry is holding more tenders in order to slow this growth and lower costs, but yields will rise further," said Wojciech Labryga, fixed income dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
Dealers did not expect large amounts of foreign bids on Monday, as stable interest rate prospects and no expectations of zloty gains in future months cooled investor inerest.
"Foreigners are rolling over their zloty instruments, but Polish T-bills are not attracting large amounts of new cash," said Wojciech Kowalczyk of Bank Handlowy SA.
Players expect the yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill to rise to about 21.65 percent from Wednesday's 21.56 percent.
They said the yield of the 26-week paper should increase to around 21.55 percent from the previous 21.49 percent and the shortest 13-week bill yield to 21.00 percent from 20.91. @
Dealers said Polish corporates would also not place large bids on Monday as many were were selling their T-bills in secondary trade this week to free up cash.

Some dealers said one-day rates on the money market have slipped far below the National Bank of Poland's main 14-day drainage rate of 22.15 percent because the central bank wanted to help the finance ministry sell treasuries.

"The central bank may have allowed rates to fall and kept the market overliquid in order to create larger demand for T-bills and help out the finance ministry," said one dealer at a large Polish bank.
Dealers said one-day rates should remain around 21.50 percent in the early stages of next week -- the last counted in this month's reserve period, which ends on Sunday, June 29.
"No large rate movement can be expected on Monday and Tuesday, with rates holding flat at Friday's levels," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz, chief dealer at PKO BP.
Tomorrow/next rates ended at 21.30/21.60 percent on Friday.
The zloty was expected to drift around 1.5 percent from the parity rate next week with little hope that the central bank would allow it to strengthen further, dealers said.

They said the zloty's upside was limited after this week's capital inflow into Bank Handlowy's initial public offering, estimated at around $210 million, failed to sustain the zloty above its weeks-old resistance at 1.5 percent.
On Friday the zloty was fixed at at 1.49 percent from parity, up from last week's close at 1.46 percent.
